title: Unknown Venetian envoy to the Doge (Ser.mo Principe), 29 April 1628 (DECODE R1862)

documents.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Venezia, IT ASVe 0045 010 (Serie) Busta 27 f. 354; DECODE R1862

plaintext.source: No decipherment in the record; key rebuilt from the sibling R1874, whose contemporary decipherment is imaged with it.

transcription.source: Transcribed here from the four DECODE images (no DECODE transcription on the record).
transcription.notes: Made here from the four images, then checked line by line against them with the key in hand (five passes). Two rows of page 2 had been blended from two physical lines and one row was a phantom; found by tracking baselines.

system.summary: Numerical syllabary: prefix = vowel (6 a, 51 e, 62 i, 53 o, 64 u), final two digits = consonant; plus single letters, word codes and paragraph marks.
system.sibling_key: R1874 (Mocenigo, Madrid 1628), key rebuilt from its contemporary decipherment
system.notes: 698/5198/5199 mark the edges of ciphered passages, as 6499 does in R1874. Key order: a tabular vowel x consonant grid, the consonant columns roughly alphabetical (07 b, 08 c, 10 d, 11 f, 13 g, 19 l, 20 m, 21 n, 22 p, 24 qu, 27 r, 28 s, 33 t, 37 v, 38 z). No key for this cipher survives: the known plaintext used to recover it was the chancery's contemporary decipherment of a different letter in the same cipher (R1874), aligned to its own ciphertext here.

prior_solution.where: CSP Venice vol. 21 calendars no Rome despatch of 29 Apr 1628; not in Tomokiyo or Bonavoglia.

conditions.human_role: Posed the target from the catalogue; DECODE account cookie.

solution.what: Fetched the four images with the stored DECODE cookie; the record has no transcription.
CSP Venice vol. 21, 23-30 April 1628: only the London despatch of 29 April is calendared; this letter is not.

Group-exact transcription of R1862 by an agent (digit shapes b=6, s=5, hook=2, >=7, g=9; 5-forms "s3"=53, "si"=51). The R1874 transcription agent stopped (ambiguous hand); DECODE's own R1874 transcription used instead.
Transcribed R1874's contemporary decipherment (images 8955-8959, paragraphs 5-16, ~4,800 letters) as known plaintext.

Soft-EM forward-backward alignment of R1874 code groups (DECODE transcription, 5-forms unmerged: '21'=51, '13'=53) to the decipherment, 5 segment pairs, 2,398 groups; first run with nulls allowed collapsed, rerun with 1-4 letters per group converged.

Key is a vowel x consonant syllabary: prefix 6=a, 51=e, 62=i, 53=o, 64=u; final pair 08 c,10 d,11 f,13 g,18 h,19 l,20 m,21 n,22 p,24 qu,27 r,28 s,33 t,37 v,38 z; single letters 680 a, 6280 e, 6480 i, 5190 o; words 670 che, 672 con, 5374 per, 6249 il.
R1874 key applied unchanged to R1862 page 1: continuous Italian ('ricercavo con intiera confidenza', 'serenissima republica').
Key applied to all four pages; nomenclator codes read from context (5384 qual(che), 5331 sto, 5373 part, 5387 quel, 537 ro, 6477 poc, 6240 ave, 5347 papa, 6481 stri).
Agents re-checked every line against the images with the key (glyph calibration: final n-shape = 2, 7 = long-tailed >, 9 = g), correcting digit slips and group splits.
Five image passes over the transcription with the key in hand; found and fixed two rows blended from two physical lines and one phantom row on page 2.
LM hill-climb over key values for weak/unknown groups.
Pages 1, 3 and 4 and the first half of page 2 read continuously; 20 word-code tokens and page 2 lines 18-28 left unread.
Swept the DECODE API for every ASVe record: the Codice Amadi (Inquisitori di Stato reg. 1269, 14 key records) and the Busta 4 key registers are 16th-century or earlier and hold no key of this type.
The word codes are alphabetical within each prefix row's blocks (53: papa 47, part 73, per 74, piu 77, qual 84, quel 87, ques 88), which brackets every open code.

Second round of image passes: word codes read from context and bracket (6274 molto, 5140 dov, 673 cose, 5323 pro, 5117 gre, 5208 co, 5174 far, 5347 papa), key corrections 628 sa, 6439 signor, 6481 i; one manuscript line on page 3 found untranscribed and transcribed (P3 L26b, 'la prego non nominarme').

Read fraction measured two ways: 91.3% of code groups stand in lines that score as Italian (line level, neighbour-context), 86.4% by a 25-character sliding window; 15 group tokens (1.2%) still have no value.

Final image round on the last garbled spans: 'se Palma sara ben fortificata, quanto presidio aveva', 'il disgusto di Aquileia', 'in strettissima confidenza', 'havuto particolar notitia', 'et qua et altrove', 'Mantova et di Savoia', 'esprimersi'.

Key values proved against the letter: 634 tra, 5132 stre, 683 a (Aquileia), 5388 quest, 5386 quant, 5189 glie, 61 fat, 6212 fri (Friuli); 6443 returned to the open list as its sibling value came from a mis-split stretch.
Read bar checked three ways: 0.95 line-level with neighbour context, 0.92 by a 25-character window, 0.96 by hand audit; 12 tokens (0.9%) still have no value.

P1 L07-08 re-checked on the image: 5349 read as papali from its alphabetical place after 5347 papa (I); 6202 'bi' before 'instanza' read as a one-digit slip for 6222 'pi' = più (I). Key file unchanged.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1268 tokens, 153 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -1.965 per letter; random keys -3.023 (z 12.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.332 (mean -2.349, z 38.8); annealer on the real text -2.291. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcription tx/groups.txt and decipherment tx/plain.txt; effective key written from decode.py to texts/key.tsv, with this letter's overrides key_over.json (base key ../r1874/key2.json)

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026): tx/R1862_reading.md marks the clear passages with ⟨ ⟩ and leaves the cipher unmarked; the clear passages were removed and the rest of the Reading section counted, 545 words. Holes: the twelve unvalued word-band codes (vo[51708]lari and [5370]i among them), eighteen [?word], co[n], [a]lcun, cardina[le], [g]loria (letters the cipher does not have), the eight words with the clerk's one-digit slips (key rebuilt here, so the slip rule does not apply), and the line P2 L22 (14 groups, sized as about 6 words, an estimate). Abbreviation expansions of the cipher's own sp (Sp[agnuo]li, Sp[agna], Spa[gna]) counted read. Result: read share 0.953 -> 0.912 (497/545; 0.920 with P2 L22 as one bare mark); R1862 and the target move from read to read in part; fraction_read (0.991 of groups valued) and fraction_coherent (0.95, line measure) unchanged.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.959; polyphony 0.005; 12 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.291

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt here by EM alignment of a different letter, DECODE R1874 (Mocenigo, Madrid, ASVe Busta 30), with its contemporary decipherment, and then applied to R1862 (Busta 27, Rome), where about 30 word codes were added from context and alphabetical order and three values corrected.
outcome.notes: Key rebuilt from the sibling R1874 by EM alignment, then extended from context and from the alphabetical order of the word band. 99.1% of the code-group tokens have a value. Share reading as sense: 0.95 measured line by line against a period Italian model with neighbour context (measure.py), 0.92 by a stricter 25-character sliding window (measure_tok.py), 0.96 by a hand audit token by token. The clerk's own one-digit encipherment slips are recorded in key_over.json _slips and read through, as his spelling slips (sivoia, germinia, voro) are.

gaps.detail: R1874's decipherment does not cover that band of the key, no other letter in this cipher survives on DECODE, and the ASVe key registers that do (Codice Amadi reg. 1269, Busta 4 regs. 8/16/18) are a century older. Their alphabetical brackets are recorded in NOTES.

gaps.item: one line, P2 L22 (14 groups), image-true after four independent readings and still giving no sense
gaps.detail: every group in it is a structural grid value, so it turns on a clerk's slip or a word outside the corpus; exhaustive single- and double-substitution searches returned nothing

gaps.item: words counted unread in the cipher-word share (16 Nov 2026): eighteen [?word] readings, four letters the clerk left out (co[n], [a]lcun, cardina[le], [g]loria) and eight words with his one-digit code slips
gaps.detail: written so on the image (sixteen image passes); the slips are read through with a key rebuilt here, which the one-digit-slip rule does not cover; settling them needs the chancery's own key or another copy of the despatch, neither of which survives on DECODE or in the ASVe key records
he does not name himself; CSP Venice vol. 21 calendars no Rome despatch of 29 Apr 1628

texts.label: Venetian ambassador at Rome to the Doge, 29 April 1628, ASVe Busta 27 f. 354 (DECODE R1862)
texts.summary: The ambassador reports his audience with Cardinal Francesco Barberini, who had twice asked whether Palmanova was well fortified and garrisoned and whether the Pontebba pass was secured; the Cardinal's view that the Emperor has too much to do at home and that Wallenstein would not come to Italy without his whole army; and the ambassador's urging that the Pope send a legate to settle the interests of Mantua and Savoy. The opening of the War of the Mantuan Succession.
texts.note: Read share over cipher words only (16 Nov 2026): tx/R1862_reading.md, everything in the Reading section outside the ⟨ ⟩ clear passages, 545 cipher words, 48 unread: the twelve unvalued word-band codes (two inside words, vo[51708]lari and [5370]i), eighteen [?word] doubtful readings, four words with a letter the cipher does not have (co[n], [a]lcun, cardina[le], [g]loria), the eight words carrying the clerk's one-digit code slips (key_over.json _slips: esprimersi, confidenza, altrove, cosi, Mantova, considerati, piu, preparati; the key is rebuilt here, not the surviving period key, so README's one-digit-slip rule does not apply), and the unread line P2 L22 sized at about 6 words (14 groups at the letter's 2.4 groups per word; an estimate; 0.920 if it is counted as one bare mark). Sp[agnuo]li, Sp[agna] and Spa[gna] expand the clerk's abbreviation sp written in the cipher and count as read; the closing ellipsis is the end of the cipher, not a hole. Recorded 0.953 before (whole reading, clear passages included).
